A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GSNO/SHNet study. The main text, equations, six figures, thirteen tables and Appendices A–F are readable and can be reliably matched.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original SSWE simulation experiments, WeatherBench forecasting, HCP dMRI evaluations, ablations and computational measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including numerical model comparisons, ablations and computational measurements in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The GSNO construction and correction term in Equations 15–20, SHNet architecture and Appendix B.2 implementation remain unchanged. The revised SHNet name is a terminology correction.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same SSWE dynamics, WeatherBench forecasting and HCP FOD angular-super-resolution tasks. No dataset, population or input scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained throughout, including expanded-channel SFNO and spatial position-embedding SNO in Table 3, and SSMT-CSD, FOD-Net, FOD-SFNO and ESCNN in Table 4. Appendix comparisons also retain their methods.

E3.justification: Splits, sample counts, resolutions, training settings and forecast horizons match, including the HCP 20/5/5 subject split. Equation 41 newly documents the existing dMRI ACC metric; it does not establish a changed evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: The block/architecture ablations in Tables 2 and 8, capacity and positional-embedding controls in Table 3, and original/correction-term ablations in Table 11 and Figure 6 are retained with the same evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same ± reporting in the experimental tables. Neither adds run counts, seeds, uncertainty explanations, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative prediction figures are unchanged. For example, SHNet's WeatherBench ACC remains 91.5%, 72.4% and 52.5% at 1, 3 and 5 days in Table 2; FOD-GSNO retains 0.9083 white-matter and 0.8517 whole-brain ACC in Table 4.

T1.justification: Before Equation 13, v2 explicitly assumes square-integrability of the Green's function; v3 removes this condition while retaining the expansion and derivation. The general L2 preliminaries and Appendix A/B.1 proofs remain, so this is a limited change to stated assumptions.

C1.justification: The central Green's-function framework, GSNO, SHNet and comparative-performance claims are retained. The abstract's added geometry-preservation wording already appears elsewhere in v2, and the conclusion rephrases the same contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the correction term, longer-horizon behavior and computational trade-offs are retained. Appendix D preserves the same generalization caveats; changing future 'datasets' to 'scenarios' adds no substantive limitation.

D1.justification: v3 adds a GSNO repository address in the abstract and Appendix E, replacing the acceptance-contingent release statement; Appendix E still describes release prospectively. It also adds Equation 41 and coefficient explanations for the existing dMRI ACC, although the printed denominator repeats the estimated-coefficient factor.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and cited works are unchanged. The revised conclusion preserves the existing positioning as a generalized framework for spherical operator design.

P1.justification: Limited edits affect the abstract, Section 4.1, metric explanation and conclusion. Appendix B.2 aligns SHNet's expanded name with the main text; the overall section structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 6 and Table 10 are reordered around the added equation, and Table 11 moves from page 21 to page 22. Local spacing and pagination change, while all figure images and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The repository address and naming corrections help, but v3 removes the explicit assumption supporting Equation 13 and introduces an apparent ACC normalization error in Equation 41: both denominator factors use g rather than distinct reference and estimated coefficients. These localized losses in mathematical and evaluation-documentation precision outweigh the limited documentation benefits; the underlying empirical evidence remains unchanged.
